newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans rekindle love for cinema - survey.
newsitem.headline: Germans rekindle love for cinema - survey.

text.p: After years when Germans avoided movie theatres in droves, the cinema is enjoying a heyday not seen in almost two decades, a study released on Tuesday showed.

More than seven percent of Germans over 14 years old see a movie at least once a week, according to the Allensbacher Market and Advertising Media Analysis (AWA 97) by the Institute of Opinion Polling.

"Cinema is in again," the institute said in a statement. "It looked like cinema was dying out in the late 1970s and the entire 1980s," it said, putting this largely down to the popularity of television and video rentals.
The institute suggested that the rebound during the 1990s might ironically be due to the increasingly wide range of channels and programmes offered on television.
"Unlike in the past, people cannot talk to each other about what they watched on television because everyone is watching something different," the institute said.
"Those people who go to see the latest Woody Allen film know that they will be able to find people with whom they can discuss it."

In 1997, 7.3 percent of Germans went to a film at least once a week, compared with 6.7 percent in 1995. Among 30 to 49-year-olds, the number who visit a cinema weekly jumped three percentage points between 1995 and 1997 to 28.3 percent.
During the same period, weekly cinema-goers between the ages of 20 and 29 dropped to 37.4 percent from 41.9 percent.
Nearly 20,000 people over 14 years old were surveyed in the AWA 97, the institute said.
